name: 1 Thessalonians

overview.author: The apostle Paul, with Silvanus (Silas) and Timothy (1:1).
overview.date: About AD 50–51, from Corinth, making it one of Paul’s earliest letters.
overview.audience: The young church in Thessalonica, a major city in Macedonia, mostly Gentile converts who had turned from idols.
overview.setting: Paul had been forced to leave Thessalonica after a few weeks because of persecution (Acts 17:1–10). Timothy brought back a good report, along with questions about believers who had died.
overview.purpose: To encourage a persecuted young church, defend Paul’s sincere ministry, urge holy living, and comfort them with the hope of Christ’s return and the resurrection.
overview.structure: Thanksgiving and Paul’s ministry among them (1–3), and instructions on holiness, love, the Lord’s coming, and church life (4–5).

items.title: The dead in Christ and the Lord’s coming

themes.title: Faith, Love, and Hope
themes.text: Paul remembers their work of faith, labor of love, and steadfastness of hope (1:3).

themes.title: Turning to God
themes.text: They turned from idols to serve the living and true God.

themes.title: Genuine Ministry
themes.text: Paul was gentle like a nursing mother and shared his own life.

themes.title: Holiness
themes.text: God’s will is your sanctification, including sexual purity.

themes.title: The Lord’s Return
themes.text: Christ will descend, the dead will rise, and we will always be with the Lord.

themes.title: Readiness
themes.text: The day of the Lord comes like a thief, so stay awake and sober.

themes.title: Joyful Community
themes.text: Rejoice always, pray without ceasing, give thanks in all circumstances.

keyVerses.quote: You turned to God from idols to serve the living and true God.
For this is the will of God, your sanctification.
And so we will always be with the Lord.
Rejoice always, pray without ceasing, give thanks in all circumstances.
He who calls you is faithful; he will surely do it.

christInBook.text: Jesus, raised from the dead, delivers us from the wrath to come.
Because Jesus died and rose, God will bring with Him those who have fallen asleep.
The Lord Himself will descend from heaven with a cry of command.
Christ died for us so that whether awake or asleep we might live with Him.

crossReferences.note: The founding of the Thessalonian church.
The resurrection at the last trumpet.
Like a thief in the night.

reflection: Paul remembered their work of faith, labor of love, and steadfast hope. Which of these is strongest in you, and which is weakest?
What “idols” have you turned from, or still need to turn from?
How does Paul’s gentle, self-giving ministry (2:7–8) model how to care for others?
How does the hope of 4:13–18 shape the way you grieve?
Which of the short commands in 5:12–22 do you most need to practice this week?

chapterList.title: A Model Church
chapterList.summary: Paul thanks God for the Thessalonians’ work of faith, labor of love, and steadfastness of hope. The gospel came to them not only in word but in power and the Holy Spirit. They received it in much affliction with joy and became an example to believers everywhere, turning from idols to serve God and wait for His Son from heaven.
questions: What do faith, love, and hope look like in action (1:3)?
How did the gospel come to them (1:5)?

chapterList.title: Paul’s Ministry Among Them
chapterList.summary: Paul reminds them that his ministry was not from deceit or flattery or greed. He was gentle like a nursing mother and cared like a father, sharing not only the gospel but his own life. They received God’s word as truly God’s word. Paul longs to see them; they are his glory and joy.
questions: What motives did Paul reject in ministry (2:3–6)?
How do the mother and father images describe good spiritual care?
What does it mean to receive Scripture as God’s word (2:13)?

chapterList.title: Timothy’s Good Report
chapterList.summary: Unable to bear it, Paul sent Timothy to strengthen them in afflictions, which believers are destined for. Timothy returns with good news of their faith and love, and Paul is comforted: “Now we live, if you are standing fast in the Lord.” He prays that their love would increase and their hearts be established in holiness.
questions: Why does Paul say suffering should not surprise believers (3:3–4)?
Pray Paul’s prayer in 3:12–13 for someone you love.

chapterList.title: Holiness and the Coming of the Lord
chapterList.summary: Paul urges them to please God more and more. God’s will is their sanctification: abstaining from sexual immorality and controlling their bodies in holiness. They should love one another, live quietly, and work with their hands. Believers who have died will not miss out: the Lord will descend, the dead in Christ will rise first, and “we will always be with the Lord. Therefore encourage one another.”
questions: What does God’s will for your sanctification involve (4:3–8)?
Why is a quiet, hardworking life a witness (4:11–12)?
How does 4:13–18 give hope in grief?

chapterList.title: Children of the Day
chapterList.summary: The day of the Lord will come like a thief in the night, but believers are children of light. So stay awake and be sober, wearing faith, love, and the hope of salvation. God has destined us for salvation, not wrath. Respect leaders, admonish the idle, encourage the fainthearted, help the weak. “Rejoice always, pray without ceasing, give thanks in all circumstances.” God will sanctify you completely.
questions: What does it mean to be a child of the day (5:4–8)?
How can you rejoice, pray, and give thanks in all circumstances?

tagline: Faith, love, and hope while waiting for the Lord’s return
readingPlan: 5 chapters: one chapter a day takes 5 days; two a day takes about 3 days. For each chapter, read it on ESV.org, then come back here for the summary, questions, and your notes.
